newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn urges Germans to leave Cambodia, suspends aid.
newsitem.headline: Bonn urges Germans to leave Cambodia, suspends aid.

text.p: Germany on Thursday urged its citizens to leave Cambodia as soon as possible and suspended development aid, condemning the overthrow of Prince Norodom Ranariddh by rival co-premier Hun Sen.
"The putsch contradicts all democratic and legal principles and the Cambodian constitution of 1992," Development Minister Carl-Dieter Spranger said in a statement.

"Due to the unsatisfactory security situation in Cambodia, the Foreign Ministry advises all Germans in Cambodia to leave by the next possible civilian flight or by land, as long as this is possible without danger," a foreign ministry statement said.
The ministry advised Germans who decided to stay on to move to the capital Phnom Penh, at least for the moment.
Spranger's ministry said the German government would agree on any further actions concerning Cambodia within the European Union and the international aid community.
Germany restarted aid to Cambodia in 1992 and has given 119 million marks ($67 million) since then, donating 17.6 million marks in 1996, the ministry said. ($ = 1.763 German Marks)
